CausalChain: Chronic biliary inflammation and cholestasis -> Activation of CAFs and ECM remodeling -> Increased ECM stiffness -> Activation of mechanotransduction pathways (YAP/TAZ) -> Synergistic enhancement by IL-6–STAT3 signaling -> Epigenetic modifications of cholangiocytes -> Acquisition of cancer stem cell traits and chemoresistance
Hypothesis: In cholangiocarcinoma, CAF-induced ECM stiffening cooperates with IL-6–STAT3 signaling to activate YAP/TAZ-mediated epigenetic reprogramming in cholangiocytes, fostering a cancer stem cell phenotype that underlies chemoresistance and aggressive tumor progression.
Abstract: Recent studies in cholangiocarcinoma have unveiled a complex interrelationship among chronic inflammation, stromal remodeling, and epigenetic reprogramming. Here, we propose that the desmoplastic, stiffened extracellular matrix (ECM) created by activated cancer‐associated fibroblasts (CAFs) in an inflammatory microenvironment synergizes with pro‐inflammatory IL-6–STAT3 signaling to activate mechanotransduction pathways, such as YAP/TAZ, within cholangiocytes. This dual activation drives epigenetic modifications that promote cancer stem cell properties and contribute to the chemoresistant phenotype of cholangiocarcinoma. This hypothesis highlights a novel convergence point linking ECM mechanics and inflammatory signaling to epigenetic reprogramming, offering a new perspective on therapeutic intervention in this aggressive tumor.
